source.title: Efficacy and Safety of Dapagliflozin According to Background Use of Cardiovascular Medications in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial

source_inconsistencies.issue: All-three background-medication subgroup differs between abstract/narrative and Figure 2.
source_inconsistencies.abstract_report: n=4,243; CV death/HHF HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.62-0.93); kidney-specific composite HR 0.62 (0.44-0.87).
source_inconsistencies.figure_2_report: n=3,654; CV death/HHF HR 0.75 (0.59-0.94); kidney-specific composite HR 0.70 (0.48-1.02).
source_inconsistencies.handling: Both source assertions were retained as independently anchored atoms and marked needs_review; no silent reconciliation was made.

extraction_limitations: The retrieved Drive folder contained the primary article and Supplement 1 (protocol/SAP) only.
Supplement 2, which the article cites for additional eTables/eFigures including body weight, HbA1c, and diastolic blood pressure analyses, was not available and therefore could not be reconciled.
Supplement 3, referenced for the Data Sharing Statement, was not available.

The 189-page protocol/SAP was semantically sampled for load-bearing trial-design and analysis-plan assertions rather than atomized line-by-line; non-load-bearing administrative and shipping appendices were excluded.
schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated field for treatment-by-subgroup interaction P values; these are preserved in canonical statements/tags.
The schema does not explicitly model publication lineage between a secondary analysis and its underlying trial protocol/SAP; provenance, supplement locators, and tags are used.
The schema cannot directly encode endpoint-definition evolution across protocol and later secondary analysis beyond separate anchored atoms.
